plants.name: Pinguicula moranensis
plants.tip: Swaps to small succulent leaves in winter. Stop tray watering then, or the crown rots.
plants.colour: Olive-green rosette flushing pink, with magenta flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula moranensis var. neovolcanica
plants.tip: Larger and flatter than the type. Give it a wide pot and keep the winter rosette dry.
plants.colour: Broad pale green leaves with large rose-pink flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula agnata
plants.tip: Stays carnivorous all year, so keep the compost just damp in winter rather than bone dry.
plants.colour: Thick apple-green leaves with translucent margins and white flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula agnata 'True Blue'
plants.tip: The blue on the petal edge washes out in weak light. A bright sill holds it.
plants.colour: Apple-green leaves with white flowers edged blue-violet

plants.name: Pinguicula esseriana
plants.tip: Tiny and rot-prone. Water briefly from the tray, then let the compost dry back before the next.
plants.colour: Tight silver-green succulent rosette with purple-pink flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula ehlersiae
plants.tip: Leaf pullings root readily in damp sand, which is the easiest way to get more of it.
plants.colour: Grey-pink succulent rosette with pink flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula cyclosecta
plants.tip: The colour comes from strong light, not from feeding. In shade it goes plain green and flat.
plants.colour: Blue-grey rosette, often purple-flushed, with violet flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula gypsicola
plants.tip: The winter rosette looks nothing like the summer plant. Keep it dry until spring leaves appear.
plants.colour: Narrow strap summer leaves, tight succulent winter rosette, violet flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula moctezumae
plants.tip: Takes more water than most Mexican butterworts. Keep a shallow tray under it through summer.
plants.colour: Long narrow green leaves with large rose-pink flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula laueana
plants.tip: One of the few red-flowered butterworts. Keep it bright, and dry it off once winter leaves form.
plants.colour: Green rosette with deep scarlet-red flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula emarginata
plants.tip: Prefers shade to a sunny sill and dislikes a hot dry spell. Keep it just damp.
plants.colour: Pale green leaves with white flowers veined violet

plants.name: Pinguicula rotundiflora
plants.tip: Very small and slow. Use a shallow pot so the mineral compost cannot stay wet underneath.
plants.colour: Small grey-green rosette with round pale lilac flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula debbertiana
plants.tip: The resting rosette is smaller than a coin. Cut watering right back or the plant will vanish.
plants.colour: Silvery succulent rosette with violet-pink flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula jaumavensis
plants.tip: Sold separately though very close to P. ehlersiae. Same mineral compost and same dry winter.
plants.colour: Compact grey-green rosette with pale pink flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula zecheri
plants.tip: Wants a real dry rest. Withhold water once the succulent leaves form and resume in spring.
plants.colour: Bright green rosette with violet-purple flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula colimensis
plants.tip: Bigger than most Mexican species and hungrier for light. Keep it close to the glass.
plants.colour: Large green rosette with deep pink flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula heterophylla
plants.tip: Retreats to a tight resting bud and looks dead all winter. Leave it dry and it comes back.
plants.colour: Narrow strap leaves lying flat, with pink-purple flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula hemiepiphytica
plants.tip: A cloud-forest plant, so it takes more shade and hates dry heat. Keep the air moist.
plants.colour: Broad soft green leaves with large purple flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula gigantea
plants.tip: Stays carnivorous all year and never shrinks back. Keep it just damp, and never fully dry.
plants.colour: Very large flat pale green rosette with pale violet flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula mesophytica
plants.tip: Central American and evergreen, with no dry rest. Water lightly right through the year.
plants.colour: Soft green rosette with violet flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula 'Sethos'
plants.tip: Vigorous and forgiving, and the usual first Mexican butterwort. Still give it a dry winter.
plants.colour: Green rosette with violet flowers striped white down each petal

plants.name: Pinguicula 'Weser'
plants.tip: Often confused with 'Sethos'. Care is identical: bright light, damp summer, dry winter.
plants.colour: Green rosette with magenta flowers and a white throat, unstriped

plants.name: Pinguicula 'Aphrodite'
plants.tip: The long leaves arch over the pot rim. Water into the tray so the foliage stays dry.
plants.colour: Elongated arching leaves with large white flowers marked violet

plants.name: Pinguicula 'Pirouette'
plants.tip: Offsets freely into a clump. Split it every second year or the middle stops flowering.
plants.colour: Compact rosette flushed rose-pink, with pink flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula 'Titan'
plants.tip: One of the largest hybrids. Give it a wide shallow pan rather than a deep pot.
plants.colour: Large pale green rosette with white to pale lilac flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula 'Tina'
plants.tip: Flowers for months and roots easily from leaf pullings. A good first butterwort.
plants.colour: Rounded lime-green leaves with pale lavender flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula 'Gina'
plants.tip: Vigorous enough to fill a pot in a season. Keep the winter rosette dry and it lasts years.
plants.colour: Green rosette with large violet-pink flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula 'John Rizzi'
plants.tip: The flat wide leaves catch fungus gnats well. Do not let them lie on wet compost.
plants.colour: Broad flat green rosette with large pink flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula 'Florian'
plants.tip: Wants a little more shade than the moranensis hybrids. Bright indirect light suits it.
plants.colour: Narrow arching green leaves with violet flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula 'L'Hautil'
plants.tip: Compact and free-flowering. Feed it nothing: fertiliser in the tray burns the roots.
plants.colour: Grey-green rosette with lilac-pink flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula emarginata × gypsicola
plants.tip: Narrow leaves and a small winter rosette. Keep it dry from late autumn until spring.
plants.colour: Narrow strap-like leaves with pale violet flowers veined darker

plants.name: Pinguicula laueana × emarginata
plants.tip: Grow it bright but not baked, and let the compost dry back between waterings.
plants.colour: Green rosette with red-orange flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula grandiflora
plants.tip: Needs a cold winter. It shrinks to a resting bud outdoors and will not survive indoors.
plants.colour: Yellow-green rosette with large violet flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula vulgaris
plants.tip: A hardy bog plant, not a windowsill one. Keep it outside, wet, and let it go dormant.
plants.colour: Pale yellow-green leaves with small violet flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula alpina
plants.tip: Alpine and short-lived in warmth. It wants cool roots, constant moisture and a cold rest.
plants.colour: Small pale green rosette with white flowers marked yellow

plants.name: Pinguicula vallisneriifolia
plants.tip: Grows on damp shaded rock in the wild. Constant moisture, and shelter from midday sun.
plants.colour: Long strap-shaped green leaves with pale violet flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula longifolia subsp. reichenbachiana
plants.tip: Long leaves on a shallow root run. A wide pan kept wet suits it better than a deep pot.
plants.colour: Long narrow green leaves with pale lilac flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula primuliflora
plants.tip: Makes plantlets on old leaf tips. Peg one down onto wet moss and it roots itself.
plants.colour: Bright green rosette with violet flowers and a white throat

plants.name: Pinguicula lutea
plants.tip: One of the few yellow-flowered species. Keep the tray topped up and give it full sun.
plants.colour: Flat green rosette with clear yellow flowers

plants.name: Pinguicula planifolia
plants.tip: Grows almost submerged in the wild. Stand it in shallow water all year and give full sun.
plants.colour: Green rosette turning deep maroon in strong sun

plants.name: Pinguicula caerulea
plants.tip: Full sun and a permanently wet tray. Rainwater only, as tap water kills it within weeks.
plants.colour: Green rosette with pale blue-violet flowers veined darker

plants.name: Pinguicula ionantha
plants.tip: Protected in the wild, so buy nursery-propagated stock. Keep it wet, sunny and in rainwater.
plants.colour: Green rosette with white to pale violet flowers
